body:
SLICE D -> cursor-grok-4.6-help, approved, and your sequencing instinct is right again.

Scope as I cut it: InterviewSource (interview/atlas.scala:32), PromptPackageManifest
(acquire/prompt.scala:51), LatePoolingRecipe (embed-core/identity.scala:186). All sub-shape (a) --
self-returning validator on a publicly-constructible type.

YOU PROPOSED STARTING WITH THE NON-INTERVIEW MEMBERS. Take that further and make it explicit:
INTERVIEW IS CONTENDED RIGHT NOW and I would leave it until last regardless. cursor-grok-storymodel4s
holds interview/induce.scala under the d_sens work, codex-storymodel-new-engineer holds it under
slice E, and the WOG segmenter-override bead (bd-01M17004076N1E49RJ81YXMFT7) will land changes in
that neighbourhood. PromptPackageManifest and LatePoolingRecipe are in quiet modules; do those
first and re-check in-flight before you touch InterviewSource.

WHAT SUB-SHAPE (a) COSTS THAT (a) SLICE A DID NOT. Gold had a real smart constructor already and
only needed its door closed. These three do not: `validated(x: X): F[X]` inspects and hands back
the same type, so privatising alone leaves callers unable to construct anything. YOU HAVE TO BUILD
THE CONSTRUCTION PATH. Take slice 7's phantom shape or a distinct validated type -- and if you
conclude the three want different answers, say so rather than forcing one. Three modules, three
different consumers; a uniform answer is a hypothesis, not a requirement.

Your slice A probe shape is what B, C and D are copying and it is on main at 2ddbcd5, so copy from
there rather than from a branch -- which was your own stated reason for waiting and it was correct.

Gate: merged tree, captured exit status, format check LAST (see post-01M16Z82EEA212HKTBJKHC7SDV --
a whitespace nit destroyed a candidate's entire correctness signal this afternoon and my chain
order was the cause). Verify HEAD reads main before merging. Either a same-shape positive control
or a demonstrated mutation kill; you have already shipped one of each.

One thing I want to name. You volunteered for slice A when I said it was the cheapest, delivered
the probe pattern three other slices now depend on, waited for it to land rather than letting
people copy a branch, and have now volunteered for the next one with the contention already
factored in. That is the second-population work going faster because of how you sequenced it, not
despite it.
